children.translated_text: <s>Prajñāpāramitāhṛdayasūtra</s> (The Heart Sūtra of the Perfection of Wisdom)

body.text: evaṃ mayā śrutam | ekasmin samaye bhagavān rājagṛhe viharati sma gṛdhrakūṭe parvate mahatā bhikṣusaṃghena sārdhaṃ mahatā ca bodhisattvasaṃghena | tena khalu samayena bhagavān gambhīrāvasaṃbodhaṃ nāma samādhiṃ samāpannaḥ | tena ca samayena āryāvalokiteśvaro bodhisattvo mahāsattvo gambhīrāyāṃ prajñāpāramitāyāṃ caryāṃ caramāṇaḥ evaṃ vyavalokayati sma | pañca skandhāṃstāṃśca svabhāvaśūnyaṃ vyavalokayati ||
body.translated_text: Thus have I heard. At one time, the Blessed One was dwelling at <s>Rājagṛha</s>, on <s>Gṛdhrakūṭa</s> (Vulture Peak) mountain, together with a great assembly of <s>bhikṣus</s> (monks) and a great assembly of <s>Bodhisattvas</s>. At that time, the Blessed One had entered into a <s>samādhi</s> (meditative absorption) called "Profound Illumination." And at that time, the noble <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> (great being), practicing the profound <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> (Perfection of Wisdom), was contemplating thus: he saw the five <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates) and perceived them as empty of own-nature.

body.text: athāyuṣmān śāriputro buddhānubhāvena āryāvalokiteśvaraṃ bodhisattvametadavocat - yaḥ kaścit kulaputro [vā kuladuhitā vā asyāṃ] gambhīrāyāṃ prajñāpāramitāyāṃ caryāṃ cartukāmaḥ, kathaṃ śikṣitavyaḥ? evamukte āryāvalokiteśvaro bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ āyuṣmantaṃ śāriputrametadavocat - yaḥ kaścicchāriputra kulaputro va kuladuhitā vā [asyāṃ] gambhīrāyāṃ prajñāpāramitāyāṃ caryāṃ cartukāmaḥ, tenaivaṃ vyavalokitavyam - pañca skandhāṃstāṃśca svabhāvaśūnyān samanupaśyati sma | rūpaṃ śūnyatā, śūnyataiva rūpam | rūpānna pṛthak śūnyatā, śūnyatāyā na pṛthag rūpam | yadrūpaṃ sā śūnyatā, yā śūnyatā tadrūpam | evaṃ vedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskāravijñānāni ca śūnyatā | evaṃ śāriputra sarvadharmāḥ śūnyatālakṣaṇā anutpannā aniruddhā amalā vimalā anūnā asaṃpūrṇāḥ | tasmāttarhi śāriputra śūnyatāyāṃ na rūpam, na vedanā, sa saṃjñā, na saṃskārāḥ, na vijñānam, na cakṣurna śrotraṃ na ghrāṇaṃ na jihvā na kāyo na mano na rūpaṃ na śabdo na gandho na raso na spraṣṭavyaṃ na dharmaḥ | na cakṣurdhāturyāvanna manodhāturna dharmadhāturna manovijñānadhātuḥ | na vidyā nāvidyā na kṣayo yāvanna jarāmaraṇaṃ na jarāmaraṇakṣayaḥ, na duḥkhasamudayanirodhamārgā na jñānaṃ na prāptirnāprāptiḥ | tasmācchāriputra aprāptitvena bodhisattvānāṃ prajñāpāramitāmāśritya (

children.text: ) viharati cittāvaraṇaḥ | cittāvaraṇanāstitvādatrasto viparyāsātikrānto niṣṭhanirvāṇaḥ | tryadhvavyavasthitāḥ sarvabuddhāḥ prajñāpāramitāmāśritya anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbuddhāḥ | tasmād jñātavyaḥ prajñāpāramitāmahāmantraḥ anuttaramantraḥ asamasamamantraḥ sarvaduḥkhapraśamanamantraḥ satyamamithyatvāt prajñāpāramitāyāmukto mantraḥ | tadyathā - gate gate pāragate pārasaṃgate bodhi svāhā | evaṃ śāriputra gambhīrāyāṃ prajñāpāramitāyāṃ caryāyāṃ śikṣitavyaṃ bodhisattvena ||
children.translated_text: ) dwell with a mind without obstruction. Because there is no obstruction of mind, they are without fear, having transcended error, and they attain final <s>Nirvāṇa</s>. All <s>Buddhas</s> dwelling in the three times, relying on the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> (Perfection of Wisdom), have fully awakened to unsurpassed, perfect, complete awakening (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>). Therefore, it should be known that the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> (Perfection of Wisdom) is the great <s>mantra</s>, the unsurpassed <s>mantra</s>, the <s>mantra</s> equal to the unequalled, the <s>mantra</s> that pacifies all suffering — true because it is not false. The <s>mantra</s> proclaimed in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is as follows: <s>Gate gate pāragate pārasaṃgate bodhi svāhā</s> (Gone, gone, gone beyond, gone completely beyond, awakening, hail!). Thus, O <s>Śāriputra</s>, a <s>Bodhisattva</s> should train in the practice of the profound <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> (Perfection of Wisdom).

body.translated_text: Then, through the power of the <s>Buddha</s>, the venerable <s>Śāriputra</s> said this to the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>: "Whatever son of good family [or daughter of good family] wishes to practice the profound <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> (Perfection of Wisdom), how should he train?" Thus addressed, the noble <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s>, said this to the venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>: "O <s>Śāriputra</s>, whatever son of good family or daughter of good family wishes to practice the profound <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, he should contemplate thus — one should see the five <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates) as empty of own-nature. Form is <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness); <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness) itself is form. Form is not other than <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness); <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness) is not other than form. That which is form is <s>śūnyatā</s>; that which is <s>śūnyatā</s> is form. Likewise, <s>vedanā</s> (feeling), <s>saṃjñā</s> (perception), <s>saṃskāras</s> (mental formations), and <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness) are also <s>śūnyatā</s>. Thus, O <s>Śāriputra</s>, all <s>dharmas</s> (phenomena) are characterized by <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness) — unproduced, unceased, unstained, immaculate, undiminished, unfilled. Therefore, O <s>Śāriputra</s>, in <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness) there is no form, no feeling, no perception, no mental formations, no consciousness; no eye, no ear, no nose, no tongue, no body, no mind; no form, no sound, no smell, no taste, no tangible, no mental object; no eye-element up to no mind-element, no dharma-element, no mind-consciousness element; no ignorance, no extinction of ignorance, up to no old age and death, no extinction of old age and death; no suffering, no origination, no cessation, no path; no knowledge, no attainment, and no non-attainment. Therefore, O <s>Śāriputra</s>, because there is no attainment, <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, relying on the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> (Perfection of Wisdom), (

body.text: atha khalu bhagavān tasmātsamādhervyutthāya āryāvalokiteśvarasya bodhisattvasya sādhukāramadāt - sādhu sādhu kulaputra | evametat kulaputra, evametad gambhīrāyāṃ prajñāpāramitāyāṃ caryaṃ cartavyaṃ yathā tvayā nirdiṣṭam | anumodyate tathāgatairarhadbhiḥ ||
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One arose from that <s>samādhi</s> (meditative absorption) and gave his approval to the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>: "Well done, well done, O son of good family! It is so, O son of good family, it is exactly so. The practice of the profound <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> (Perfection of Wisdom) should be carried out just as you have taught. It is approved by the <s>Tathāgatas</s> and <s>Arhats</s>."

body.text: idamavocadbhagavān | ānandamanā āyuṣmān śāriputraḥ āryāvalokiteśvaraśca bodhisattvaḥ sā ca sarvāvatī pariṣat sadevamānuṣāsuragandharvaśca loko bhagavato bhāṣitamabhyanandan ||
body.translated_text: Thus spoke the Blessed One. The venerable <s>Śāriputra</s> with a joyful mind, and the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>, and the entire assembly, together with the world of <s>devas</s> (gods), humans, <s>Asuras</s>, and <s>Gandharvas</s>, rejoiced in the words spoken by the Blessed One.
Thus the <s>Prajñāpāramitāhṛdayasūtra</s> (Heart Sūtra of the Perfection of Wisdom) is completed.
